title: Kernel failure-mode mapping and telemetry manifest
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a canonical mapping of serving runtime kernel failure modes to observable signals, the telemetry schema required to detect each class, an experimentation and profiling playbook for reproducing and triaging, additions to the benchmarking suite to validate mitigations, and a short incident runbook for field response. The goal is to reduce MTTD/MTTR for kernel-related degradations and provide a reproducible experiment surface for safety rollouts.

Scope: kernel execution layer and scheduler interactions within the Redwood inference runtime (GPU kernels, slot scheduler, KV cache layer, kernel handoff glue). Does not include control-plane orchestration (cross-region routing) except where it directly affects kernel affordances (e.g., fallback translation).

Ownership and SLAs

- Primary owner_team: engineering (serving-runtime).
- Secondary stakeholders: eng-sre (oncall), eng-infra (GPU fleet), security-and-compliance (if PII surfaced during traces).
- Detection SLA: new kernel regressions should be detectable via automated telemetry within 5 minutes of an SLO breach signal (tail-latency > 99.9th baseline).

Failure modes taxonomy (high-level)

1) Slow kernel (increased p99–p999 latency)
   - Cause examples: regressed kernel code-path, contention on tensor cores, thermal throttling.
   - Observables: rising kernel_exec_latency percentiles, increased GPU occupancy variance, drop in token throughput, tail-latency drift on specific request classes.

2) Kernel hang / watchdog-triggered node fail
   - Cause examples: deadlock in kernel work-queue, NV driver regression, interconnect stall.
   - Observables: missing kernel completion events, CPU spin loops on dispatch threads, NVML/TDX node-level stalls, abrupt eviction traces.

3) Silent correctness degradation (numerical drift / quantization mismatch)
   - Cause examples: quantization kernel change, dtype mismatch, kernel reorder.
   - Observables: model output divergence vs baseline on shadow channel, increased invalid-token rates, eval-suite QA failures on golden prompts.

4) Resource mis-accounting (memory leak / fragmentation)
   - Cause examples: allocator regression, orphaned buffers across handoffs, fragmenting NVLink buffers.
   - Observables: sustained growth in GPU_alloc_bytes, higher OOM counts on soft-gc, increased allocator fragmentation ratio.

5) Backpressure amplification (scheduler oscillation)
   - Cause examples: credit accounting bug, admission controller mis-synthesis.
   - Observables: cyclical admission/revocation, queue-depth oscillation, correlated spike in rejection_rate and tail-latency.

Canonical telemetry signals and minimum schema

The runtime telemetry must carry both event and aggregated timeseries signals to map failures quickly. Below is the minimal set required for each failure mode. Operators should extend with local labels (region, topo_id, kernel_variant) for richer triage.

Table: signal | type | retention recommended | key dimensions
| kernel_exec_latency_ms | timeseries histogram | 90d at coarse, 30d at full-resolution | service, kernel_id, model_family, priority, slot_id |
| kernel_submit_event | event (trace) | 30d | trace_id, request_id, kernel_variant, args_hash |
| kernel_complete_event | event (trace) | 30d | trace_id, request_id, duration_ms, return_code |
| gpu_occupancy_pct | timeseries | 90d | gpu_unit, host, instance_type |
| allocator_free_bytes | timeseries | 90d | heap_name, slot_id |
| nvml_thermal_celsius | timeseries | 30d | gpu_unit, host |
| kvcache_hit_rate_prefix | timeseries | 90d | model_family, session_cohort |
| shadow_eval_delta_score | timeseries | 365d (for regression hunting) | prompt_set, model_variant |

Signal naming and invariant: every kernel-level event must include a kernel_id, kernel_variant, and a monotonic timestamp_ns. Events should be linkable to a request_id or to a synthetic shadow_id for benchmarked traces.

Profiling & experiment playbook (step-by-step)

1) Reproduce in shadow channel
   - Mirror a 1–5% production sample to a shadow pool tagged with the affected kernel_variant. Ensure no traffic is returned to users.
   - Capture full trace for kernel_submit_event -> kernel_complete_event and keep raw GPU profiling (nvprof or CUPTI) for at least one failing trace.

2) Isolate cohort and workload shape
   - Use request tagging to identify sequence_length, sampling_temperature, and model_family. Group by these to find shape-sensitive regressions.

3) Kernel microprofiling
   - Run microbenchmarks (single-operator synthetic runs) using the runtime microprobe harness. Sweep batch sizes, sequence lengths, dtype (fp16, bf16, int8) and collect per-kernel cycles, achieved occupancy, L2 hit rates.

4) Controlled perturbation
   - Use the controlled-kernel-perturbation harness: ramp kernel concurrency (1->N), inject temporary GPU thermal load, and simulate NVLink latency skew to observe failure thresholds.

5) Deterministic bisecting
   - If regression introduced in a recent rollout, perform a binary search across kernel build artifacts using the release manifest. Use shadow channels and run the fidelity eval-set on each midpoint.

6) Validate mitigation in bench-suite
   - Add the reproducer to the benchmarking suite (catalog entry with args), run full-suite including mixed-workload SLO simulation, and verify regression is resolved across target hardware variants.

Benchmarks to add (proposal)

- microprobe-oscillatory-load: synthetic oscillation profiles to exercise scheduler crediting under cyclical arrival patterns.
- fragment-drift-run: long-run allocator stress to detect slow-growing fragmentation within 24–48 hours.
- shadow-fidelity-sweep: golden prompt sweep across quant+kernel combinations to catch silent correctness regressions.

Release-note checklist for kernel rollouts

1) Include exact kernel ABI/hash and compatible runtime commit.
2) List all known compatible GPU families and excluded hardware.
3) Provide expected perf delta ranges by sequence_length and batch_size (p50/p95/p99).
4) Document fallback/failopen policy (if kernel fails, which variant is chosen).

Short incident runbook: kernel slow path (pseudocode)

1) Pager fires (p99 kernel latency > threshold for 5m).
2) Triage: pull the last 100 kernel_submit_event traces grouped by kernel_id. If the majority show increased internal steps, tag as kernel-slow.
3) Mitigate: route new requests to fallback kernel_variant or lower-fidelity model variant via route policy for affected cluster.
4) Remediate: collect nvprof slices from a warm replica, perform microprobe runs, and if a fast fix exists (config tweak: reduce concurrency, change CUDA stream affinity), apply in a limited canary.
5) Postmortem: record root cause, signal mapping, benchmark delta, and change the bench-suite to include the reproducer.

Common triage heuristics (quick checks)

- If nvml_thermal_celsius is rising concurrent with occupancy drops -> thermal throttling suspect.
- If kernel_complete_event missing across many traces but submit events present -> hang / watchdog path.
- If shadow_eval_delta_score shows high variance but latency normal -> correctness/regression not performance.
- If allocator_free_bytes trending down steadily across nodes -> memory leak or fragmentation.

Quality gates and automated detection rules (examples)

- Alert rule: kernel_exec_latency_ms{kernel_id="k1"}.p99 > baseline_p99(k1) * 1.3 for 10 minutes -> create SEV2.
- Auto-action: on SEV2 for kernel slow path, enact routing policy to shift 10% of traffic to fallback variant and create an automated diagnostic job to sample 250 traces to shadow store.

Data retention and privacy notes

- Traces may contain prompt hashes and request metadata. Store full traces only in restricted buckets. Telemetry summaries (percentiles) can be internal. When sharing with third parties or including in vendor bug reports, minimize user-identifying fields and use prompt_set IDs instead of raw prompts. Security must approve any full-trace export.

Open known issues & mitigations (short catalog)

- Intermittent nvlink timeout under sustained cross-GPU KV cache prefetching (mitigation: serialize prefetch window and increase nvlink retry backoff).
- Subtle int8 path reordering causing off-by-one token errors in legacy kernels (mitigation: promote failing input set to shadow-fidelity-sweep and disable int8 variant until fix).
- Scheduler-label flapping when admission credits are recomputed under heavy churn (mitigation: apply 5s smoothing to credit recomputation).

Appendix: example CLI commands and snippets

- Capture a single failing trace (from operator machine):
  rdwctl trace capture --request-id <id> --output /tmp/trace-<id>.json --include-gpu-profiling

- Run microprobe for a kernel variant:
  ./microprobe --kernel-id k_matmul_v2 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seq-lens 8,64,512 --dtype fp16 --out /tmp/mprobe.csv

- Add reproducer to bench-suite (example manifest snippet):
  name: fragment-drift-run
  description: allocator fragmentation stress run to detect slow leaks
  runtime_args: --duration 48h --pattern gaussian-bursts --seed 42

Related pages and references

- See kernel-telemetry-adoption-roadmap for rollout priorities and telemetry rollout templates.
- See controlled-kernel-perturbation-playbook for the perturbation harness and safety limits.

Next actions (short list)

- (1) Service owners: ensure minimal telemetry signals are emitted by 2026-03-01.
- (2) Bench team: onboard three reproducer profiles into the public bench-suite by 2026-04-01.
- (3) SRE: implement the two automated detection rules and the fallback auto-action by 2026-03-15.
